## Context  chord/src/context/index.ts
used by: durable-effect, env-effect; durable-rivet-effect via SqliteStorage
/** Immutable invocation-scoped values passed explicitly through operations. */
export interface Context {
	readonly abortSignal: AbortSignal | undefined;
	readonly telemetry: TelemetrySpan;
	value<T>(key: ContextKey<T>): T | undefined;
	toString(): string;
}

## ContextKey  chord/src/context/index.ts
used by: durable-effect via Context, durable-rivet-effect via SqliteStorage, env-effect via Context
/** Typed identity for one value carried by a {@link Context}. */
export interface ContextKey<T> {
	readonly token: symbol;
	/** Type-only marker that prevents keys with different value types from being interchangeable. */
	readonly valueType?: (value: T) => T;
}

## Draft  chord/src/delta/draft.ts
used by: durable-effect; durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask
/** A mutable transaction-scoped view of a JSON value, preserving tuple positions. */
export type Draft<T, Depth extends readonly unknown[] = []> = Depth["length"] extends 8
	? T
	: T extends null | boolean | number | string
		? T
		: T extends (...args: never[]) => unknown
			? T
			: T extends object
				? { -readonly [Key in keyof T]: Draft<T[Key], [...Depth, unknown]> }
				: T;

## Op  chord/src/delta/index.ts
used by: durable-effect via WatchCall, durable-rivet-effect via SqliteStorage
/**
 * Tuples are the form — in memory, on the wire, on disk.
 *
 * `r` is the ONLY op that replaces a whole value. `s`/`d`/`a`/`t` cannot target
 * the root: the type forbids it. `p` and `m` may, because a tracked value can
 * itself be an array. Operation shape is not canonical: an array may be emptied by either
 * a replacement or a root splice.
 *
 * `Op` knows nothing about the path dictionary. Interning, id references and
 * omitted paths live in `WireOp` and exist only between `encode` and `decode`.
 */
export type Op =
	| readonly ["r", JsonValue]
	| readonly ["s", NonEmptyPath, JsonValue]
	| readonly ["d", NonEmptyPath]
	| readonly ["a", NonEmptyPath, string]
	| readonly ["t", NonEmptyPath, number]
	| readonly ["p", Path, number, number, JsonValue[]]
	/** Reorder an array in place: `new[i] = old[permutation[i]]`. */
	| readonly ["m", Path, number[]];

## Path  chord/src/delta/index.ts

export type Path = readonly Seg[];

## IsAny  chord/src/json.ts

type IsAny<T> = 0 extends 1 & T ? true : false;

## JsonRepresentation  chord/src/json.ts
used by: durable-effect via InboxItem
/** Strict-JSON representation of an application data type. Unknown payloads become JsonValue. */
export type JsonRepresentation<T> = IsAny<T> extends true
	? JsonValue
	: unknown extends T
		? JsonValue
		: T extends null | boolean | number | string
			? T
			: T extends readonly (infer TItem)[]
				? JsonRepresentation<TItem>[]
				: T extends object
					? { [TKey in keyof T]: JsonRepresentation<T[TKey]> }
					: never;

export type JsonValue = null | boolean | number | string | JsonValue[] | { [key: string]: JsonValue };

## RegistryValue  chord/src/registries/registry.ts
used by: durable-effect via registryReader
/**
 * A registry's composed value as a reader of one version sees it (`self.registry`, `host.registry`): a native
 * watchable; `.value` is the last good composition (a later throwing `compose` keeps it), a watch gets each new one.
 */
export interface RegistryValue<V> extends NativeWatchable<V> {
	/**
	 * A synchronous observer of its compositions (as Durable's `observeXXX`): `advance` runs inside the batch that
	 * composed, so it only records; an attached observer counts as watching, so the composition runs for it.
	 */
	observe(observer: NativeObserver<V>, context: Context): NativeObservation<V>;
}

## SqliteDatabase  chord/src/sqlite/database.ts
used by: durable-effect, durable-rivet-effect
/**
 * Minimal portable SQLite database facade.
 *
 * All operations are asynchronous so adapters may execute outside the caller's runtime.
 *
 * `transaction` passes the callback a transaction handle. All work in the transaction
 * must use that handle; the handle is invalid after the callback settles. Adapters must
 * queue unrelated operations and other transactions until the transaction finishes. The
 * returned promise settles after commit or rollback. Calling the database itself (including
 * `transaction` or `close`) from inside a callback therefore waits for that transaction and
 * never settles.
 *
 * When the callback rejects, the adapter must roll the transaction back before rejecting
 * with that same error. If rollback fails, it must reject with a different error (for
 * example an `AggregateError`) so callers cannot mistake the callback error for a
 * guaranteed rollback.
 */
export interface SqliteDatabase extends SqliteExecutor {
	transaction<T>(callback: (transaction: SqliteExecutor) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
	close(): Promise<void>;
}

## SqliteExecutor  chord/src/sqlite/database.ts
used by: durable-effect, durable-rivet-effect
/**
 * Asynchronous SQL operations shared by a database and its transaction handles.
 *
 * `exec` runs SQL text without bindings and may contain several statements. `run`, `get`, and `all`
 * execute one statement with positional bindings. `runCounted` runs one like `run` and resolves with the rows it
 * inserted, updated or deleted, as SQLite's `changes()` counts them (index writes and rows changed by triggers do not
 * count); it may cost a statement more than `run`, so callers that need no count use `run`. Adapters may cache
 * prepared statements by SQL text, so callers pass values as bindings instead of interpolating them.
 */
export interface SqliteExecutor {
	exec(sql: string): Promise<void>;
	run(sql: string, ...params: SqliteValue[]): Promise<void>;
	runCounted(sql: string, ...params: SqliteValue[]): Promise<number>;
	get<T extends object>(sql: string, ...params: SqliteValue[]): Promise<T | undefined>;
	all<T extends object>(sql: string, ...params: SqliteValue[]): Promise<T[]>;
}

## SqliteValue  chord/src/sqlite/database.ts
used by: durable-effect, durable-rivet-effect
/** Values supported by the portable SQLite drivers. */
export type SqliteValue = null | number | bigint | string | Uint8Array;

## NativeObservation  chord/src/state/native-source.ts
used by: durable-effect via registryReader
/** What `observe` gives: the value the observer starts at, and how to detach it (Durable's `Observation`). */
export type NativeObservation<T> = { readonly value: T; detach(): void };

## NativeObserver  chord/src/state/native-source.ts
used by: durable-effect via registryReader
/**
 * A synchronous observer of a native source (Durable's observer shape): `advance` is called inside the batch that
 * changed the source, so it only records; `end` once, when the source ended (`ended`) or the observer's context was
 * aborted (`aborted`).
 */
export interface NativeObserver<T> {
	/** The source's call of this batch: its new value, or a failure it may recover from. */
	advance(call: NativeWatchCall<T>, context: Context): void;
	/** The observer is detached for good with `end`. */
	end(end: WatchEnd): void;
}

## NativeWatchable  chord/src/watch.ts
used by: durable-effect via registryReader
/**
 * An in-process value that changes and can be watched (it may hold anything, errors and functions included): a change
 * is a new value by identity, delivered without ops.
 */
export interface NativeWatchable<T> {
	/** The current value. */
	readonly value: T;
	/** A watch holding the current value, then one frame per new value; aborting the context ends it. */
	watch(context: Context): Promise<NativeWatchHandle<T>>;
}

## NativeWatchCall  chord/src/watch.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** One call of a native watch's listener: the new value, or a failure its source may recover from, as in `WatchCall`. */
export type NativeWatchCall<T> =
	| { readonly kind: "value"; readonly value: T }
	| { readonly kind: "failed"; readonly error: unknown };

## NativeWatchHandle  chord/src/watch.ts
used by: durable-effect via registryReader
/**
 * Serialized observation of an in-process value: as `WatchHandle`, but each new value is its own call, in order, without
 * ops.
 */
export interface NativeWatchHandle<T> {
	/** Acquisition value before start; latest delivered value afterward (a `failed` call keeps it). */
	readonly value: T;
	/** Install the sole asynchronous listener. Never invokes it inline. */
	start(listener: (call: NativeWatchCall<T>, context: Context) => Promise<void>): void;
	/** Idempotently stop future callbacks and return this watch's terminal result. */
	stop(): Promise<WatchEnd>;
	/** Settle when the watch terminates; an already-running callback remains caller-owned. */
	readonly closed: Promise<WatchEnd>;
}

## WatchCall  chord/src/watch.ts
used by: durable-effect; durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask
/**
 * One call of a JSON watch's listener, and one frame a source hands its watch, tagged by `kind`:
 *
 * - `value`: the newest value, the ops that turn the previous value into it, and whether the document the watch follows
 *   was retired since the previous value call. A retirement does not end the watch: `value` is then what the address
 *   shows after it (the source decides; a Durable document keeps the last value the watch was given, with no ops), and a
 *   document created there later arrives as `[["r", value]]`, possibly in the same call.
 * - `failed`: the source cannot compute its value now, with `error`; the watch stays open, and the next value arrives as
 *   `[["r", value]]`. `WatchHandle.value` keeps the last value.
 *
 * Plain data: the frame's context is the listener's second argument, never part of the call.
 */
export type WatchCall<T> =
	| { readonly kind: "value"; readonly value: T; readonly ops: readonly Op[]; readonly retired: boolean }
	| { readonly kind: "failed"; readonly error: unknown };

## WatchEnd  chord/src/watch.ts
used by: durable-effect; durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask
/**
 * Terminal result of one watch, tagged by `kind`. A watch ends only for good; a failure its source recovers from is a
 * `failed` call (`WatchCall`), and the watch stays open.
 *
 * - `stopped`: `stop()` was called.
 * - `aborted`: the context the watch was acquired with was aborted.
 * - `ended`: the source closed (its owner ended or closed).
 * - `listener_error`: the listener threw or rejected with `error`.
 * - `failed`: the source failed for good with `error`.
 */
export type WatchEnd =
	| { readonly kind: "stopped" | "aborted" | "ended" }
	| { readonly kind: "listener_error"; readonly error: Error }
	| { readonly kind: "failed"; readonly error: unknown };

## WatchHandle  chord/src/watch.ts
used by: durable-effect; durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask
/**
 * Serialized observation of an immutable value: one listener call at a time; changes made meanwhile arrive folded into
 * the next call.
 */
export interface WatchHandle<T> {
	/** Acquisition revision before start; latest delivered immutable revision afterward (a `failed` call keeps it). */
	readonly value: T;
	/** Install the sole asynchronous listener. Never invokes it inline. */
	start(listener: (call: WatchCall<T>, context: Context) => Promise<void>): void;
	/** Idempotently stop future callbacks and return this watch's terminal result. */
	stop(): Promise<WatchEnd>;
	/** Settle when the watch terminates; an already-running callback remains caller-owned. */
	readonly closed: Promise<WatchEnd>;
}
